findings.problem: The top decoder has no drawn output path to epsilon_theta. The black output arrow instead starts at the top Cross Attention box, whose drawn input is the condition bus and which has no U-Net feature/query input. The observed graph has a c-to-output path and no x_t-to-output path.
findings.why_material: The figure can teach a condition-only noise predictor, contrary to the article contract epsilon_theta(x_t,t,c). In conditional cross-attention, U-Net features supply Q and encoded condition supplies K/V.
findings.minimal_correction: Keep a continuous decoder-feature-to-prediction-head path; show image-feature Q and condition K/V entering cross-attention on that feature path. Route the resulting feature into the later decoder/output, rather than exporting a condition-only side branch.
findings.evidence: connection-counterexamples.json:unet; actual original pixels were inspected

findings.problem: Random t points only into Fixed Formula. The Trainable Denoiser receives only x_t; the mandatory separate time-conditioning input is absent.
findings.why_material: The same x_t value occurs at different noise levels with different optimal epsilon targets. For independent unit-normal x0 and epsilon, fixing x_t=1 gives E[epsilon|x_t,t]=sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t): 0.316227766 at alpha_bar=.9 versus 0.948683298 at .1. A predictor of x_t alone cannot represent both.
findings.minimal_correction: Draw the same sampled t into the denoiser/time-embedding input in addition to the forward noising formula. Keep epsilon target and prediction paths separate from the sampling state update.
